message: Got it, thanks. Two quick things to pin down. Is the $8,000 a month before taxes? And do any of the adults have a job that offers a health plan (even if you don't sign up for it)? If you're not sure, your pay stub or benefits sheet usually says so.
reply: Around $8,000 a month. No idea, honestly.

summary: Household: Indiana, 5 people (2 adults, 3 children, one under 5), about $96,000/year gross earnings from work, no self-employment, no pregnancy or disability, no other income reported. Likely eligible: CHIP for the children (income is near Indiana's CHIP limit, so it needs verification), Child Tax Credit (refundable part, since they have earned income and three children), and ACA premium tax credit if no affordable job-based coverage is available. Not eligible on income: SNAP, WIC, school meals, EITC, Medicaid, TANF, SSI. Hand off to a caseworker to confirm the household's income figures and whether any adult has job-based health coverage that was offered, which the household could not answer.
